newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Racal shares slump on new pft warning.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Racal shares slump on new pft warning.

text.p: Britain's Racal Electronics Plc issued its second profit warning within six months on Friday, telling investors annual profits would be above 40 million pounds ($65.3 million) after another poor period for data products.

The figure was well below analysts' expectations, with year profit forecasts pitched between 41 million and 75 million pounds, averaging at 53.5 million. The news could now trigger a wave of fresh forecast downgrades.
This second profit warning follows Racal's setback in December, ahead of its first half results when it warned that profits would be substantially below market expectations.
On Friday, shares repeated last December's reaction by plunging 33 pence to 244 -- a fall of 12 percent which took the shares to a year low of 240 pence at one stage.

In a statement, Racal said, "The company announces that the data products group has regrettably not achieved the modest profit expected in the second half of (the) financial year 1996/97 and will, in fact, incur a second half loss in the region of seven million pounds."
It blamed the loss on the delayed launch of its fast frame relay product, resulting in more research and development costs and lower anticipated revenues.
Racal added that the data products unit had been restructured and achieved cost cuts.

In the year 1996/1997, 38 million was spent on R&D within the unit. The two other main group businesses, managed network services and defence electronics, performed well, however and had "excellent prospects ahead," said Racal.

But investors took small comfort in this after suffering as recently as December when Racal told the market first half profits would be around 21 million pounds -- nearly 20 million below expectations. That time round Racal blamed its radio group.
That first warning triggered a profit downgrade from the 65-94 million range for annual profits. The 41-75 million range now looks set for another revision in light of Friday's news.
Racal's results are due on June 3.

The group has already been under severe pressure to improve returns to shareholders. Recent press reports speculated that Racal chairman and founder Ernest Harrison was considering a break-up of the group through disposals, mergers and management buyouts.
Some analysts believe it could offer more value split apart than bound together.

Justinian Clifford-Bowles, analyst at Credit Lyonnais Laing, said "They are not making an adequate return on sales and this is just going to put more pressure on Harrison to increase value to shareholders."
